membership.title: Join as a Member of the Friends
membership.intro: Annual member subscriptions provide essential funding for practical conservation equipment, woodland care, path maintenance, and our community campaign.

tiers.description: Covers all adults living at the same address, demonstrating united household support.

support_impact.heading: What does your membership support?
support_impact.p1: The funds we raise have financed many projects over the years, such as major clearance, new paths, purchasing tools and key equipment, and supporting conservation projects alongside the Conservators.
support_impact.p2: Some of our members join the committee, and some take an active part in practical conservation and volunteer work. From litter-picking and clearance of invasive species to pond and rock clearance, your support helps protect this landscape for everyone.

donations.title: Make a Donation
donations.intro: One-off and regular donations fund urgent storm repairs, pond restoration, and wildlife surveys. If you are a UK taxpayer, Gift Aid increases the value of your donation by 25% at no extra cost to you.

online_giving.title: Donate Online (Card & Direct Debit)
online_giving.text: Make an immediate, secure one-off gift via GoCardless to support urgent conservation, path restoration, and habitat care across our 256 acres.
online_giving.custom_note: For custom or larger donation amounts, please use a direct bank transfer (see details alongside).

direct_giving.title: Bank Transfer or Cheque
direct_giving.intro: If you prefer not to donate online, you can transfer funds directly to our charity account or post a cheque.

legacy_banner.title: Legacy Giving in Your Will
legacy_banner.alt: Ancient sandstone gorge, mossy crags and woodland canopy in Happy Valley on Tunbridge Wells Common
legacy_banner.text: A gift in your will ensures future generations will experience the wild beauty and quiet solace of the Commons. Even a modest legacy creates a lasting conservation endowment for ancient trees, sandstone rocks, and footpaths.

volunteering.title: Volunteering on the Commons
volunteering.intro: Practical conservation on the Commons is organised and led by The Commons Conservators, caring for the land under the 1890 Act. The Friends actively support these efforts, funding tools and equipment and encouraging community involvement.

image_card.title: Practical Conservation Mornings
image_card.text: From litter-picking and invasive species clearance to scrub control and pond care, volunteer mornings offer a friendly way to spend time outdoors while making a tangible difference to our commons.
image_card.footer: Tools and guidance provided by the Commons Conservators.

join_card.title: Join a Volunteer Morning
join_card.text: Sessions are open to everyone, whether you can spare an hour occasionally or wish to join regularly. No prior experience is needed.
join_card.contact_lead: For volunteering questions or to register your interest:
join_card.secondary_btn_text: View Upcoming Dates on Events Page

pledge_panel.title: Pledge to the Community Purchase Bid
pledge_panel.description: A pledge is a confidential promise of financial support to help our registered charity acquire the freehold of Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall Commons. Funds will only be requested when the community sale is legally agreed.
pledge_panel.card_intro: Every pledge—large or small—shows that our local community stands together to protect the Commons for future generations.
card_bullets: Pledges of any amount make a genuine difference
Direct email option with Trustee John Barber
